messages:
Lena R: Heads-up 1: we're planning to deprecate the legacy /v1/bulk endpoint in favor of the streaming /v2/stream API. Reason: unpredictable tail latency and much higher mem usage on multi-tenant hosts. Proposed timeline in brief: announce -> 60d grace window -> 3w certification runway -> shim support for 120d. Posting plan here for partner input.
Omar S: Thanks. Can you call out behavioral diffs so partners can scope effort? e.g., ordering guarantees, partial failures, batch size semantics.
Lena R: Yes. Short list: ordering preserved per-request (streaming sends chunked pieces), partial item-level errors now returned inline (instead of failing entire batch), we cap per-stream concurrent items to 1000 by default. Doc: https://redwood.internal/partner-ops/stream-migration (internal).
Devon (Marketplace): Question: marketplace managed partners rely on bulk semantics to control billing units. Will billing change when they move to streaming?
Taylor P: Billing model: we will map streaming fragments to tokens consumed same as generation tokens. For bulk->stream we will provide a migration multiplier guidance and a billing sandbox for partners to run migration traffic and see expected costs.
Niv (SI Partner): Our integration runs on customer gateways with 4GB memory. Streaming is attractive but we need a bridge for slow rollouts. Will you provide a translator that accepts /v1/bulk and proxies to /v2/stream?
Lena R: Yes, we'll publish a reference translator (Go and Python) that can run as a sidecar or hosted proxy. It will support two modes: "translate-async" (buffer+convert) and "translate-pass" (stream passthrough). We recommend translate-pass for partners that can stream.
Partner Ops Bot: Created channel #partner-stream-canary-1768123456 and CI job partner/migration-run-1768123456. Tests: ordering-preserve, partial-error-handling, cost-estimation, load-stability. Results posted automatically. :robot_face:
Omar S: Need to add a compatibility matrix: which features are not supported by the shim (eg. multi-model routing per item, per-item priority headers).
Lena R: Good call 1. Shim limitations will be explicit in the repo README. We'll also publish a signed binary tarball for partners who can't pull from registries.
Devon (Marketplace): For marketplace listing we need a partner-facing notice and a managed upgrade option for partners that opt in to have Redwood handle translation (for a fee). Also: is there a co-announcement cadence?
Taylor P: Marketing + Partnerships co-announcement plan: internal partner preview at T-7d, early adopter cohort invite at T-30d, public marketplace banner at T-45d. We'll draft language and share in #partner-comm-drafts.
Niv (SI Partner): Implementation Q: what about long-lived streams and timeouts? Our gateway kills connections after ~5m. If streaming responses exceed that, we'll need either chunk checkpointing or resumable streams.
Lena R: We will support resumable streams via a resume token returned at regular intervals. Spec snippet below.
```
# streaming fragment example
{ "stream_chunk": true, "seq": 42, "payload": {"tokens": "..."}, "resume_token": "rt-abc123" }
# resume flow: client reconnects with header Resume-Token: rt-abc123
```
Omar S: Please include tests for resume semantics and firewall proxies that might buffer chunked responses. Add an ev test harness scenario for 5m+ responses.
Partner Ops Bot: Canary job updated with scenario "resume-flow-sim" and will run nightly against the canary fleet.
Devon (Marketplace): Billing sandbox access request: how do partners get access?
Taylor P: We'll provision sandbox accounts tied to partner orgs. Please submit partner-sandbox request in the doc and Solutions will grant tokens.
Niv (SI Partner): Note: for air-gapped enterprise installs we'll need the translator + shim packaged with checksums. Can you confirm the release cadence for those artifacts?
Lena R: We'll produce signed tarballs on each minor release (every 2 weeks) and one GA bundle at the end of the grace window. We'll post S3 links and short-lived presigned URLs.
Omar S: Risk: if a high-volume partner leaves large batches un-sliced during migration, it could spike cost. Suggest we add a rate-limiter in the translator with safe defaults and an escape hatch to drop overly-large requests.
Lena R: Agree. Translator will enforce max_items_per_request=500 by default and return 413 with guidance to split. We'll add configuration for partners to tune.
Devon (Marketplace): Can we surface a "migration-ready" badge on the marketplace for partners who complete cert? That'll help users choose partners.
Taylor P: We'll do that. Criteria = pass cert suite + opt-in marketplace upgrade flag. Badge mockups coming.
Niv (SI Partner): For our deliverables: we'll need the shim, resume-token spec, example client code, CI tests, and the billing sandbox. We'll start onboarding two pilot customers next week.
Lena R: Great 1. I'll attach the migration checklist in the doc and tag action owners. Meeting: 45-min migration working session scheduled tomorrow (invite sent) to review the translator alpha and the certification matrix. Please add must-have test cases to the doc under "partner-migration-tests". :white_check_mark:
